name: scroll-pageup-moves-viewport
opens_with: A long transcript (200 wrapped lines) renders, then the reader pages up twice while tail-follow is active
notes: P4-1 regression pin (2026-10-09 live audit: the entire keyboard scroll ladder was dead in live sessions). The pageup keys drain before the mock content lands, but the mutation they make - auto_scroll=false + scroll_offset += 10 each - persists while content arrives paused (and the reflow-anchor reconcile grows the offset to keep the reader's chosen position), so the final frame proves the render seam: with the seam broken (pending_resize_anchor returning the per-frame chrome anchor), resize_anchor_scroll overrode user_scroll on every frame and the view stayed pinned to the tail (L199 visible, L020 not). With the one-shot wired, the view parks well above the tail: L020 visible, L199 off-screen. The keys arrive early by harness construction; that is fine because the state, not the key timing, is what the render must honor.
